metaDescription: EVIARC Sweet jackfruit is a jackfruit variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: EVIARC Sweet is a registered jackfruit variety, also sold or known as EVIARC Sweet langka or EVIARC jackfruit. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2006 as NSIC 2006 Jf 05. RIARC Satellite Abuyog bred it. Its record notes a yield of 30 to 40 mature fruits.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of EVIARC Sweet was about 19 years old and about 7 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 30 to 40 mature fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in Jun Aug. (Major Fruiting) Dec. Feb. (Minor fruiting). A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit jackfruit fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of EVIARC Sweet weighs about 12066.67 grams, and its shape is ovoid. The flesh is golden yellow and smooth and crispy. Its sweetness measured 25.14 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 42.58 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is Jun Aug. (Major Fruiting) Dec. Feb. (Minor fruiting), bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Main crop June to August, minor crop December to February, seedling jackfruit trees bear in 4 to 14 years.
**Yield:** About 30 to 40 mature fruits per tree.
**Fruit:** Ovoid, about 12 kg, yellowish green rough skin, golden yellow, smooth, crisp, juicy, fiberless bulbs, strong aroma, about 25 Brix, about 43 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a sweet Leyte jackfruit (about 25 Brix) with crisp, fiberless bulbs and a second, minor crop in December to February. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant EVIARC Sweet jackfruit

Pick a selection by flesh: firm and crisp for fresh eating and processing, or soft and sweet. Grafted trees of a named selection bear true. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is EVIARC Sweet langka the same as EVIARC Sweet?
items.a: Yes. EVIARC Sweet langka is another name for EVIARC Sweet, registered as NSIC 2006 Jf 05. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 30 to 40 mature fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of EVIARC Sweet?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
